P01-014.strongest_rejected_alternative: The single Ezek.7.5-Ezek.7.27 row, rejected on the 2mp recognition close and the doubled eye-not-sparing refrain at oshb:Ezek.7.9, whose five-word WEB rendering “My eye will not spare” (web:Ezek.7.4) stands at 7:4 and is contracted at 7:9. The WEB's own paragraph breaks inside this stretch (7:15, 7:23) may stand as a secondary, tier-4 consideration only: none of them coincides with a word-event, messenger formula or set-your-face device — they are translation-layer paragraphing — so the entire stretch still reads as one intensifying doom-poem to its own recognition-formula close at 7:27.

P02-001.literature_type_guess: temple-vision onset: the transported hand-of-YHWH scene and what the prophet is first shown, “the seat of the image of jealousy, which provokes to jealousy” (web:Ezek.8.3)
P02-001.device_notes: Category note: this row is vision_report by the transported first-person scene it narrates, not by its abomination content. P02-002.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row through 8:18 (treating all four temple-tour tableaux as one row) was weighed: the text supports it by the repeated 'again see' device running through 8:6, 8:13, 8:15 and 8:17, but a twelve-verse row (MEASURED: web:Ezek.8.7-Ezek.8.18 is 12 verses, counted on the WEB face) with no internal formula anchor at all would understate the four distinct transport-marked scenes; the transport verbs at 8:7, 8:14 and 8:16 are kept as row-opening evidence instead.

P04-011.boundary_rationale: Every reference in this row touches MT ch 21 and is written dual. Onset: the and-you-son-of-man-prophesy sub-onset at web:Ezek.21.28 = oshb:Ezek.21.33 (וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֗ם הִנָּבֵ֤א וְאָֽמַרְתָּ֙ כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֔ה אֶל בְּנֵ֥י עַמּ֖וֹן וְאֶל חֶרְפָּתָ֑ם וְאָמַרְתָּ֗ חֶ֣רֶב חֶ֤רֶב פְּתוּחָה֙ לְטֶ֣בַח מְרוּטָ֔ה לְהָכִ֖יל לְמַ֥עַן בָּרָֽק), carrying its own messenger formula and a foreign addressee — the WEB reads it “concerning the children of Ammon, and concerning their reproach” (web:Ezek.21.28 = oshb:Ezek.21.33) — an addressee-class shift from the Judean material closed just before it. Close: the emphatic I-YHWH-have-spoken formula at web:Ezek.21.32 = oshb:Ezek.21.37 (לָאֵ֤שׁ תִּֽהְיֶה֙ לְאָכְלָ֔ה דָּמֵ֥ךְ יִהְיֶ֖ה בְּת֣וֹךְ הָאָ֑רֶץ לֹ֣א תִזָּכֵ֔רִי כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבַּֽרְתִּי), with a pe immediately after.

P08-001.boundary_rationale: Onset: the word-event formula opens this unit and the parent, Ezek.33.1 וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Ezek.33.1) — one of the book's 39 strict word-event onsets and a hard seam; it also carries the P6/P7 seam at 32:32/33:1, corroborated by a pe mark following MT 32:32 (single-witness) immediately before this unit's onset, since the addressee returns from the nations “to the children of your people” (web:Ezek.33.2) in the next verse, Ezek.33.2 בֶּן אָדָ֗ם דַּבֵּ֤ר אֶל בְּנֵֽי עַמְּךָ֙ וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם אֶ֕רֶץ כִּֽי אָבִ֥יא עָלֶ֖יהָ חָ֑רֶב וְלָקְח֨וּ עַם הָאָ֜רֶץ אִ֤ישׁ אֶחָד֙ מִקְצֵיהֶ֔ם וְנָתְנ֥וּ אֹת֛וֹ לָהֶ֖ם לְצֹפֶֽה (oshb:Ezek.33.2). Close: the row ends where the watchman analogy itself ends, at Ezek.33.9 וְ֠אַתָּה כִּֽי הִזְהַ֨רְתָּ רָשָׁ֤ע מִדַּרְכּוֹ֙ לָשׁ֣וּב מִמֶּ֔נָּה וְלֹא שָׁ֖ב מִדַּרְכּ֑וֹ ה֚וּא בַּעֲוֺנ֣וֹ יָמ֔וּת וְאַתָּ֖ה נַפְשְׁךָ֥ הִצַּֽלְתָּ (oshb:Ezek.33.9), corroborated by a samekh mark following that verse (single-witness, disclosed). No recognition or utterance refrain closes this sub-unit — the close is topical, not formulaic, and is disclosed as such rather than claimed as a formula match. Both sides weighed: onset side carries the hard-seam word-event plus the addressee return; close side carries the samekh corroboration at oshb:Ezek.33.9, immediately before the topical shift at Ezek.33.10, where 'son of man' reopens with a distinct target (“the house of Israel” (web:Ezek.33.10)) and a quoted popular saying, the disputation-oracle device that opens at Ezek.33.10.

P08-010.boundary_rationale: Onset: the witness records a pe after MT 35:15 (single-witness), at the seam this unit opens on. The sub-onset 'and you, son of man' at Ezek.36.1 וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֔ם הִנָּבֵ֖א אֶל הָרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְאָ֣מַרְתָּ֔ הָרֵי֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל שִׁמְע֖וּ דְּבַר יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.36.1) pivots the shared Ezek.35.1 word-event frame from Edom “to the mountains of Israel,” (web:Ezek.36.1) the second side of a two-sided unit shared with Ezek.35.1-Ezek.35.15. A cluster of six messenger-formula occurrences runs Ezek.36.2 through Ezek.36.7 (verified directly from these verses' own bytes); this cluster does not cut internally, since the addressee (the mountains) never changes and no refrain-grade close intervenes between any two occurrences. A samekh mark falls after Ezek.36.4, mid-cluster; disclosed as non-cutting for the same reason. Close: a 2mp recognition-family clause at Ezek.36.11 וְהִרְבֵּיתִ֧י עֲלֵיכֶ֛ם אָדָ֥ם וּבְהֵמָ֖ה וְרָב֣וּ וּפָר֑וּ וְהוֹשַׁבְתִּ֨י אֶתְכֶ֜ם כְּקַדְמֽוֹתֵיכֶ֗ם וְהֵטִֽבֹתִי֙ מֵרִאשֹׁ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם וִֽידַעְתֶּ֖ם כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.36.11) (wider family, disclosed), followed by Ezek.36.12 וְהוֹלַכְתִּי֩ עֲלֵיכֶ֨ם אָדָ֜ם אֶת עַמִּ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וִֽירֵשׁ֔וּךָ וְהָיִ֥יתָ לָהֶ֖ם לְנַחֲלָ֑ה וְלֹא תוֹסִ֥ף ע֖וֹד לְשַׁכְּלָֽם (oshb:Ezek.36.12) restating the inheritance promise and a samekh mark, close the row immediately before a fresh messenger formula reopens at Ezek.36.13, itself licensed as a cutting seam by the addressee change from this row's 2mp/2ms address (“you,” the mountains) to the 2fs address (“you,” feminine singular, the land) that opens at Ezek.36.13.

P10-004.boundary_rationale: Onset side: 40:20 opens the outer court's gate circuit on a measure notice rather than a vayiqtol verb, מָדַ֥ד אָרְכּ֖וֹ וְרָחְבּֽוֹ (oshb:Ezek.40.20) 'he measured its length and its width', immediately after the outer court's whole-court span closes at 40:19. The row measures the outer north gate (40:20-23), keyed to the first gate's own dimensions, הָיָ֔ה כְּמִדַּ֖ת הַשַּׁ֣עַר הָרִאשׁ֑וֹן (oshb:Ezek.40.21) “the measure of the first gate” (web:Ezek.40.21), a phrase standing only at 40:21 in the chapter (sweep: 1 verse), and the outer south gate (40:24-27), keyed instead by כַּמִּדּ֖וֹת הָאֵֽלֶּה (oshb:Ezek.40.24) 'according to these measurements', a refrain recurring at 40:24, 40:28, 40:29, 40:32, 40:33 and 40:35 (sweep: 6 verses across chapter 40); the row carries four of the ch-40 doubled K/Q verses (40:21, 40:22, 40:24, 40:26) plus a single note at 40:25, every one the recurring ketiv-defective/qere-plene 3ms possessive-suffix pattern on chambers, posts, porches, windows and palm trees, never on the cubit figures themselves. A transport verb sits inside this row at 40:24, וַיּוֹלִכֵ֨נִי֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַדָּר֔וֹם (oshb:Ezek.40.24) “He led me toward the south” (web:Ezek.40.24), moving from the north gate to the south gate within the same outer court; it is disclosed as intra-row sub-onset texture, not the row seam, because it changes compass direction but not court. Close side: 40:27 ends the south outer gate on its hundred-cubit span to the inner court's south gate, וַיָּ֨מָד מִשַּׁ֧עַר אֶל הַשַּׁ֛עַר דֶּ֥רֶךְ הַדָּר֖וֹם מֵאָ֥ה אַמּֽוֹת (oshb:Ezek.40.27), immediately before 40:28's court-change transport verb. The seam at 40:27/40:28 turns on a location change -- the next verse's transport verb crosses from the outer court into the inner court -- unlike the compass-direction transport at 40:24 inside this row.

P10-010.boundary_rationale: Onset side: 42:1 opens with a double transport verb, וַיּוֹצִאֵ֗נִי אֶל הֶֽחָצֵר֙ הַחִ֣יצוֹנָ֔ה ... וַיְבִאֵ֣נִי אֶל הַלִּשְׁכָּ֗ה (oshb:Ezek.42.1) “he brought me out into the outer court” (web:Ezek.42.1) ... “Then he brought me into the room” (web:Ezek.42.1) -- the strongest onset in the span after 40:1 and 43:1 -- moving the tour to the priests' chambers, first north-side (42:1-9) then, by parallel description, south-side (42:10-12). Close side: 42:13-14 supplies the row's function, delivered as a genuine speak-formula, וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י (oshb:Ezek.42.13) 'he said to me': these are the holy chambers where the priests “eat the most holy things” (web:Ezek.42.13) and must change garments before approaching the people -- a law-toned close inside a measurement row, disclosed rather than reclassified. Both the double transport at onset and the speak-formula at close are tier-1 devices, a stronger onset-and-close pairing than a bare content shift would give, despite the total absence of parashah corroboration in these chapters.

P10-015.boundary_rationale: Onset side: 43:18 opens on a said-to-me verse, וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י, and then carries בֶּן אָדָם֙ כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.43.18) 'son of man, thus says the Lord YHWH' -- one of the book's 122 messenger-formula verses, and the clearest speech-onset here after the throne declaration of 43:1-9 -- introducing the altar's dedication ordinances. The utterance formula נְאֻ֛ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה (oshb:Ezek.43.19) appears mid-unit at 43:19, read as paragraph-final rather than row-final since the seven-day consecration instructions continue without interruption. The row carries the young-bull sin offering, the blood rite on the horns and corners, the second-day goat, the seven-day consecration, and closes at 43:27 on the same utterance formula, וְרָצִ֣אתִי אֶתְכֶ֔ם נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהֹוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.43.27) “Then I will accept you,’ says the Lord Yahweh” (web:Ezek.43.27), this time genuinely row-final. Close side: immediately after that utterance the verse carries two consecutive samekh marks, the sole doubled occurrence among the book's marked verses (sweep: 183 verses) -- making 43:27 the best-attested close available and the strongest evidence for ending it exactly here. Both sides converge unusually cleanly here: a messenger-formula onset opposite an utterance-plus-doubled-mark close.

P11-013.boundary_rationale: Onset: no formula device opens Ezek.48.30 (“These are the exits of the city” (web:Ezek.48.30)); the seam behind it at 48.29/48.30 is argued from the Ezek.48.29 close (utterance + pe) and the topic shift from the tribal-portion summary to the city gates. The row covers the city's four sides, their measurements and named gates (30-34), and the book's final verse (35), the city's circumference and its new name. Close: the book's own end. No formula closes 48.35; no parashah mark is recorded after it, since none is possible on the book's last verse; a paseq is recorded within it (count-only, single-witness). This is disclosed as the row's own close condition rather than argued as a gap or omission.

P01-008.boundary_rationale: Onset: 4:1 וְאַתָּ֤ה בֶן אָדָם֙ קַח לְךָ֣ לְבֵנָ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.4.1) (“You also, son of man, take a tile” (web:Ezek.4.1)), the 'and you, son of man' sub-onset that opens P2 (one of the book's 23 occurrences of that construction), immediately after the parent seam at oshb:Ezek.3.27. The same siege-tile complex continues through the lying sign-acts at 4:4 and the food-rationing at 4:9 without a matching 'son of man' sub-onset at either point (both open with the bare 've'attah' alone), so all three stages read as one commanded symbolic act rather than three. At 4:8, וְהִנֵּ֛ה נָתַ֥תִּי עָלֶ֖יךָ עֲבוֹתִ֑ים (oshb:Ezek.4.8) (“Behold, I put ropes on you” (web:Ezek.4.8)) recurs the exact word from 3:25 on the far side of the parent seam, disclosed as continuity evidence already weighed at that seam. A second address at 4:16, בֶּן אָדָם֙ (oshb:Ezek.4.16), intensifies rather than restarts the act (“behold, I will break the staff of bread” (web:Ezek.4.16)). Close: 4:17, לְמַ֥עַן יַחְסְר֖וּ לֶ֣חֶם וָמָ֑יִם (oshb:Ezek.4.17) (“that they may lack bread and water” (web:Ezek.4.17)), with a pe recorded after it, before 5:1 opens a distinct sign-act with its own 'son of man' address.
P01-008.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the tile sign-act (4:1-4:3) from the lying and food-rationing sign-acts (4:4-4:17) as two units. How the sign-acts of chs 4-7 divide is an open question, and the 4:3/4:4 seam is its strongest form. The mark on the verse before this cut is weighed as corroboration for the alternative: on the rival's far face the witness records a samekh after oshb:Ezek.4.3 (single-witness), and that verse closes on the sign-act colophon א֥וֹת הִ֖יא לְבֵ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Ezek.4.3), “This shall be a sign to the house of Israel” (web:Ezek.4.3), standing verse-final. On the rival's near face the candidate onset oshb:Ezek.4.4 carries no formula whatever: MEASURED over the pointed Hebrew witness, no verse of ch 4 belongs to the counted messenger, utterance, recognition or word-event formula classes, the chapter's only counted device verses being the son-of-man address at 4:1 and 4:16 and the year-word non-datelines at 4:5-4:6. The colophon is not a close-role formula - oshb:Ezek.4.3 is neither an utterance-formula verse (sweep: 81 verses) nor a member of the wide recognition family (sweep: 64 verses) - and the addressee is unchanged across the seam, 2ms imperatives standing to the prophet on either side. A ve'attah inside an open unit begins a sub-unit only when the addressee changes or the verse before it ends on a verse-final close-role formula; neither holds here, and a mark by itself never supplies that close. The rival is therefore paragraph-grade, held on those grounds, and the samekh is disclosed for the alternative it corroborates rather than for this row. The address forms bear this out, 4:3 included, the very verse the mark follows: the titled sub-onset וְאַתָּ֤ה בֶן אָדָם֙ stands at 4:1 and again at 5:1, whereas bare וְאַתָּ֤ה without the title opens three interior stages - 4:3, 4:4 and 4:9 - so the text stages the siege-model, the iron pan, the two lying postures and the rationed food as one commanded act and not as separate commands (oshb:Ezek.4.1).

P03-013.device_notes: Across this span there is no K/Q note and no editors' note; this witness records one paseq inside it, at MT 17:24, count-only and single witness. A samekh is recorded following MT 17:21 (single witness), marking the front-seam break that a fresh planting figure begins just after, at 17:22.

P06-009.boundary_rationale: Onset: 27:1 opens with the strict word-event formula, "וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר" (oshb:Ezek.27.1). 27:2 supplies the genre command to the prophet, "וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֔ם שָׂ֥א עַל צֹ֖ר קִינָֽה" — “take up a lamentation over Tyre” (web:Ezek.27.2, WEB) — the imperative-to-the-prophet plus קִינָֽה (oshb:Ezek.27.2) noun, the clearest lament_qinah byte-anchor in this span, in contrast to the reported-speech קִינָה֙ (oshb:Ezek.26.17) inside Ezek.26.17. In the WEB, “You, son of man, take up a lamentation over Tyre;” (web:Ezek.27.2). Close (both sides): 27:36 ends "סֹֽחֲרִים֙ בָּ֣עַמִּ֔ים שָׁרְק֖וּ עָלָ֑יִךְ בַּלָּה֣וֹת הָיִ֔ית וְאֵינֵ֖ךְ עַד עוֹלָֽם" (oshb:Ezek.27.36) with a SAMEKH immediately after and no recognition/utterance/"I YHWH have spoken" formula in the verse; the close is argued from the parashah mark plus the chapter's own colophon-like terminal clause (the WEB renders it “You have come to a terrible end, and you will be no more.”, web:Ezek.27.36, WEB), not from a formula. This is treated as ONE row for the whole chapter because a qinah-labelled unit is never split, and this region is held as one 36-verse qinah; the internal trade list at 27:12-24 is itself a list never cut inside, and no formula licenses an internal seam. A formula does stand inside the chapter, but it licenses nothing: MEASURED from the pointed Hebrew witness, the long-form messenger formula stands inside MT 27:3 (oshb:Ezek.27.3), mid-verse within the commissioned speech frame. A messenger formula marks a sub-onset in just two cases, a change of addressee or a preceding verse that ENDS on a close-role formula, and neither holds: the addressee does not change (Tyre throughout) and MT 27:2 does not END on a close-role formula. MEASURED over the same witness, that is the chapter’s ONLY internal messenger formula, and the word-event formula occurs only at the onset, MT 27:1. Behind, 26:21 closed the Tyre-siege chapter on the utterance formula + SAMEKH; ahead, 28:1 opens a fresh strict word-event onset for the prince-of-Tyre oracle.
P06-009.device_notes: WHOLE-CHAPTER SPAN (cap disclosure): 36 verses (MEASURED over the pointed Hebrew witness) against the 7-10 verses-per-row target, which is the benchmark that governs this row; the 14-16 verse allowance is NOT available here, because that allowance belongs only to the measured-and-listed blocks, named by chapter, and this chapter is not among them; held here at medium_low with the cap disclosed rather than an unmarked internal cut, since the qinah is never split and the internal trade list (12-24) is never cut inside. Three K/Q sites (27:3, 27:6, 27:15) and two OSHB editorial notes (27:27, 27:29, both the "BHS has been faithful to the Leningrad Codex" class) fall inside this span and are disclosed rather than used as boundary evidence.
P06-009.strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting at 27:11/27:12 (the shift from the ship-building description to the trade list) or at 27:25/27:26 (end of the trade list, resumption of the poetic lament proper) to bring the row nearer the 7-10 verse target was rejected: neither point carries a word-event, messenger-formula, or parashah mark, both are plain `|q` line continuations, and a qinah-labelled unit is never split, regardless of length; the size cap is disclosed instead of forcing an unmarked internal cut. That negative holds in the witness: MEASURED in this witness, no parashah mark stands on MT 27:11, 27:12, 27:25 or 27:26 - the chapter's only mark is the samekh after MT 27:36 (single-witness) - and MEASURED from the pointed Hebrew witness neither the messenger formula (chapter-internal only at MT 27:3) nor the word-event formula (only at MT 27:1) falls at any of those four points.

P08-002.strongest_rejected_alternative: The rival onset is the 'and you, son of man' (ve'attah) at Ezek.33.12, and the address there does shift from בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל at 33.10 to בְּנֵֽי עַמְּךָ֙ at 33.12 (oshb:Ezek.33.10, oshb:Ezek.33.12; WLC/OSHB, single witness). The two are titles for one audience inside one speech: the house-of-Israel title stands at 33.10, 33.11 and 33.20, the children-of-your-people title at 33:2, 33.12 and 33.17, and the chapter's own address opens at 33:2 with the second of them, so the shift is a title shift inside one addressee group and not an addressee change, and on that ground the ve'attah is not licensed here. The pe recorded on 33.11 is disclosed for the rival as a paragraph mark. Independently, cutting there would leave 33:10-11 as a two-verse row that is not a complete word-event unit, and 33:11's own close-shaped cluster cannot supply the licence the rival onset lacks -- its utterance formula stands mid-verse, at word 5 of that verse's 25, counting from the first, with independent imperatives running on after it, so 33.11 is not a close the rival could stand on, and a mark alone never carries that weight however strong the pe looks. The rival is therefore paragraph-grade, and the disputation runs on as one 'you say ... but I say' unit across 33:10-20, which is the near face on both of this row's seams.
P08-002.boundary_rationale: Onset: the sub-onset 'son of man' at Ezek.33.10 וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֗ם אֱמֹר֙ אֶל בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כֵּ֤ן אֲמַרְתֶּם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר כִּֽי פְשָׁעֵ֥ינוּ וְחַטֹּאתֵ֖ינוּ עָלֵ֑ינוּ וּבָ֛ם אֲנַ֥חְנוּ נְמַקִּ֖ים וְאֵ֥יךְ נִֽחְיֶֽה (oshb:Ezek.33.10) opens with the quoted popular saying it will refute, immediately following the samekh-marked close at oshb:Ezek.33.9. That re-address turns the speech from the prophet-directed watchman charge back to the people and is licensed as an onset, while the far face behind it carries that samekh and no formula, a mark only. An oath-plus-utterance combination follows at Ezek.33.11 אֱמֹ֨ר אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם חַי אָ֣נִי נְאֻ֣ם אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה אִם אֶחְפֹּץ֙ בְּמ֣וֹת הָרָשָׁ֔ע כִּ֣י אִם בְּשׁ֥וּב רָשָׁ֛ע מִדַּרְכּ֖וֹ וְחָיָ֑ה שׁ֣וּבוּ שׁ֜וּבוּ מִדַּרְכֵיכֶ֧ם הָרָעִ֛ים וְלָ֥מָּה תָמ֖וּתוּ בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Ezek.33.11), carrying its own pe mark; this is disclosed as close-grade material that is NOT final here, because the same disputation continues through a second 'son of man' sub-onset at Ezek.33.12 restating the principle for “the children of your people” (web:Ezek.33.12) and on through the righteous/wicked case-pairs of 33.14-19. Close: a second pe mark follows Ezek.33.20 וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֕ם לֹ֥א יִתָּכֵ֖ן דֶּ֣רֶךְ אֲדֹנָ֑י אִ֧ישׁ כִּדְרָכָ֛יו אֶשְׁפּ֥וֹט אֶתְכֶ֖ם בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Ezek.33.20), which restates the people's complaint from 33.17 -- the four pointed words לֹ֥א יִתָּכֵ֖ן דֶּ֣רֶךְ אֲדֹנָ֑י stand byte-identical in both verses (oshb:Ezek.33.17, oshb:Ezek.33.20; WLC/OSHB, single witness) -- and then adds YHWH's verdict (“I will judge every one of you after his ways” (web:Ezek.33.20)), which stands at 33.20 only and has no counterpart anywhere in 33.17, marking the disputation's true end. EXTRACTED from this witness's markup, with independent verification UNAVAILABLE, MT 33:20 carries no sof pasuq; the editors' note stands in its place, 'We read punctuation in L differently from BHS,' immediately before the pe (single witness). No boundary is argued from the absent mark, only from the pe that follows and the topical restatement it closes. That near face is a verdict clause with no formula of its own -- the discourse close of the disputation, corroborated by the pe that follows and by no formula -- while the far face past it opens the next unit on the dateline at 33:21. A close seam whose near face is a discourse close without a formula is what this row's medium_low records, whatever stands on its far face.

P09-002.device_notes: Operative-category disclosure: the 37.15-28 span is anchored as sign_act (the commanded stick action of 37.16-20), but its interpretation at 37.21-28 carries the salvation_oracle burden (gather/return, the covenant of peace at 37.26, ‘my servant David’ and ‘my sanctuary’ devices) -- a one-clause category deviation rather than a split: the pe behind it at 37.14 and the samekh closing it at 37.28 are the row's only framing marks, and the addressee stays constant across both halves. 37.16 is a doubled ketiv/qere verse: two notes on one verse, each written חברו (oshb:Ezek.37.16, ketiv), and each read as the same consonantal word under different pointing -- the first note reads חֲבֵרָ֑יו and the second חֲבֵרָֽיו, the two differing by exactly one codepoint, U+0591 HEBREW ACCENT ETNAHTA in the first against U+05BD HEBREW POINT METEG in the second (MEASURED by comparing the two readings the K/Q apparatus gives at this verse, codepoint by codepoint; WLC/OSHB, single witness), and 37.19 carries one further note on the same word (written חברו (oshb:Ezek.37.19, ketiv), read חֲבֵרָ֑יו (oshb:Ezek.37.19, Qere)); 37.22 carries a further K/Q note in this span (written יהיה (oshb:Ezek.37.22, ketiv), read יִֽהְיוּ (oshb:Ezek.37.22, Qere)). A boundary is never argued from any of these Qere readings; they are disclosed as textual-variant sites only.

P02-003.boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.8.14 וַיָּבֵ֣א אֹתִ֗י אֶל פֶּ֨תַח֙ שַׁ֣עַר בֵּית יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר אֶל הַצָּפ֑וֹנָה וְהִנֵּה שָׁם֙ הַנָּשִׁ֣ים יֹֽשְׁב֔וֹת מְבַכּ֖וֹת אֶת הַתַּמּֽוּז, a third transport (“he brought me to the door of the gate of Yahweh’s house” (web:Ezek.8.14)) opening the Tammuz-weeping tableau; a samekh follows this very verse (single-witness), which is disclosed as evidence that could instead argue a shorter row ending at 8:15 (see rejected alternative). The row is extended through a second transport at oshb:Ezek.8.16 וַיָּבֵ֣א אֹתִ֗י אֶל חֲצַ֣ר בֵּית יְהוָה֮ הַפְּנִימִית֒ וְהִנֵּה פֶ֜תַח הֵיכַ֣ל יְהוָ֗ה בֵּ֤ין הָֽאוּלָם֙ וּבֵ֣ין הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ כְּעֶשְׂרִ֥ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֖ה אִ֑ישׁ אֲחֹ֨רֵיהֶ֜ם אֶל הֵיכַ֤ל יְהוָה֙ וּפְנֵיהֶ֣ם קֵ֔דְמָה וְהֵ֛מָּה מִשְׁתַּחֲוִיתֶ֥ם קֵ֖דְמָה לַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ (the sun-worshippers, “about twenty-five men… their backs toward Yahweh’s temple” (web:Ezek.8.16)) because a cut before 8:16 would leave a row under three verses, and such a row is held only for a complete word-event unit — that ground is stated and weighed in the rejected alternative, and no mark-absence is offered for or against any seam here. Close: oshb:Ezek.8.18 וְגַם אֲנִי֙ אֶעֱשֶׂ֣ה בְחֵמָ֔ה לֹֽא תָח֥וֹס עֵינִ֖י וְלֹ֣א אֶחְמֹ֑ל וְקָרְא֤וּ בְאָזְנַי֙ ק֣וֹל גָּד֔וֹל וְלֹ֥א אֶשְׁמַ֖ע אוֹתָֽם is the wrath declaration — “I will also deal in wrath… I will not hear them” (web:Ezek.8.18) — a narrative and thematic close (the fourfold tableau's climax) rather than a recognition or utterance refrain; oshb:Ezek.9.1 opens the next scene with the loud-voiced cry that sets the executioners in motion, which is the strongest available onset-side confirmation that 8:18 is where the temple-tour proper ends.
P02-003.strongest_rejected_alternative: The live rival is a seam at 8:15/8:16, weighed here face by face and held. Its far face is the pointer close at oshb:Ezek.8.15, the third of this tour's forward-pointing 'you will again see' transitions (8:6, 8:13, 8:15); its near face, the candidate onset, is oshb:Ezek.8.16, a transport verse of the counted class (sweep: 33 verses) and one of the tour's scene seams, which fall at 8:5, 8:7, 8:14 and 8:16. The rival is therefore licensed on both faces and it is not dismissed. The row holds because a licensed driver yields a row under three verses only when it is a complete word-event unit: a cut before 8:16 leaves 8:14-8:15, which MEASURED on the WEB face is only 2 verses (the remainder 8:16-8:18 has 3) and is not a complete word-event unit. The samekh recorded on MT 8:14 (single-witness) is entered as support for the alternative it favours and no wider: a mark is recorded on the verse it stands after, so honouring it as a close would end this row at its own onset verse, 8:14, a one-verse row that is no complete word-event unit, and a section break carries corroborating weight only, ranking below every licensed driver.

P02-016.device_notes: No K/Q note or paseq falls in 13:1-9 (single-witness). P03-007.device_notes: A Ketiv/Qere note stands at MT 16:47 (oshb:Ezek.16.47, single-witness): the running text reads the ketiv עשיתי in place of the Qere עָשִׂ֑ית; no other K/Q note falls in 16:44-50. The witness records no paseq and no editors' note in this span.

P11-001.device_notes: MT 44.3 carries an OSHB 'anomalous form' editorial note, single-witness apparatus, disclosed and not argued as boundary evidence. P01-009.strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting at 5:13 or 5:15, the first two 'I Yahweh have spoken' occurrences, to shorten the unit. Rejected because neither is followed by a fresh onset device - the material after each continues the same verdict speech without a messenger formula, word-event or address restarting it - so only 5:17's occurrence is unit-final. The stronger rival, also weighed here, is the 5:4/5:5 seam, which would set the sign-act 5:1-4 against the interpretation 5:5-17. Its far face carries a PE recorded after oshb:Ezek.5.4 (single witness) and nothing further: that verse ends מִמֶּ֥נּוּ תֵצֵא אֵ֖שׁ אֶל כָּל בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל, and it is neither an utterance-formula verse nor one of the verses of the wide recognition family (sweep: 64 verses), so it does not close on a close-role formula. Its near face is genuinely strong, oshb:Ezek.5.5 carrying the messenger formula כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֔ה verse-initially, “The Lord Yahweh says” (web:Ezek.5.5). But a messenger formula counts as a sub-onset only where the addressee changes or the preceding verse has closed on a verse-final close-role formula, and neither condition holds at this seam: 5:4 addresses the prophet in the 2ms while 5:5 carries no second person at all, the shift to 2mp arriving only at 5:7 and to 2fs at 5:8; and a parashah mark cannot meet the second condition by itself. The row accordingly holds the seam on those stated grounds, and the PE is recorded as corroboration of the rival and not of this unit's onset.

The pe after 5:4 stands before the messenger formula at oshb:Ezek.5.5, and the samekh marks after 5:6 and 5:7 stand before the messenger formulae at oshb:Ezek.5.7 and oshb:Ezek.5.8; each of those three verses is one of the 122 verses carrying the long messenger formula, and each carries it verse-initially, 5:7 behind לָכֵ֞ן (oshb:Ezek.5.7) and 5:8 behind לָכֵ֗ן (oshb:Ezek.5.8). Single witness: a pe stands after MT 4:17, the mark this witness sets at the seam where this unit begins.

P01-013.boundary_rationale: Onset: 7:5 reopens with a fresh messenger formula immediately after 7:4's pe-marked recognition close — כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה (oshb:Ezek.7.5) “The Lord Yahweh says: ‘A disaster! A unique disaster! Behold, it comes.” (web:Ezek.7.5). Close: 7:9, the 2mp recognition-family close carrying an appended participle, וִֽידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה (oshb:Ezek.7.9) “Then you will know that I, Yahweh, strike.” (web:Ezek.7.9); this recognition member also carries the doubled “My eye will not spare” (web:Ezek.7.4) refrain — MEASURED at 5 verses book-wide (5:11, 7:4, 7:9, 8:18, 9:10) by a consonantal-skeleton sweep of the phrase *lo tachos eini* over the pointed Hebrew witness, the WEB contracting the clause at every one of those verses except 7:4, which is why the quotation cites web:Ezek.7.4 — the same refrain the close at 7:4 already carries, so 7:9 closes a distinct short unit before the unmarked doom-poem reopens at 7:10 with no formula of its own.

P02-005.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating all of 10:1-17 (the errand plus the wheel description) as one row was weighed, since nothing but content separates them. It was not taken because 10:9-17 is a self-contained descriptive unit in its own right and folding it in here would produce a seventeen-verse row (MEASURED: web:Ezek.10.1-Ezek.10.17 runs to 17 verses, counted verse by verse on its WEB face) with no internal anchor of any kind in an already mark-free chapter.
P02-005.boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.10.1 וָאֶרְאֶ֗ה וְהִנֵּ֤ה אֶל הָרָקִ֨יעַ֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ עַל רֹ֣אשׁ הַכְּרֻבִ֔ים כְּאֶ֣בֶן סַפִּ֔יר כְּמַרְאֵ֖ה דְּמ֣וּת כִּסֵּ֑א נִרְאָ֖ה עֲלֵיהֶֽם opens the throne-like sapphire vision with no transport verb and no formula at all — the scene continues directly from 9:11 with a bare 'then I looked, and behold'. The row is anchored instead on the glory's own movement: oshb:Ezek.10.4 וַיָּ֤רָם כְּבוֹד יְהוָה֙ מֵעַ֣ל הַכְּר֔וּב עַ֖ל מִפְתַּ֣ן הַבָּ֑יִת וַיִּמָּלֵ֤א הַבַּ֨יִת֙ אֶת הֶ֣עָנָ֔ן וְהֶֽחָצֵר֙ מָֽלְאָ֔ה אֶת נֹ֖גַהּ כְּב֥וֹד יְהוָֽה records כבוד יהוה rising from the cherub to “the threshold of the house” (web:Ezek.10.4; sweep: 9 verses book-wide carry כבוד יהוה — 1:28, 3:12, 3:23, 10:4, 10:18, 11:23, 43:4, 43:5, 44:4, the departure/return arc), the first stage of the glory's exit. Close: oshb:Ezek.10.8 וַיֵּרָ֖א לַכְּרֻבִ֑ים תַּבְנִית֙ יַד אָדָ֔ם תַּ֖חַת כַּנְפֵיהֶֽם — the hand of a man under the cherubim's wings — closes the coal-taking errand before the row turns to the extended wheel description. Both sides: a samekh follows oshb:Ezek.9.11 immediately before this row's onset (single-witness), giving Masoretic corroboration to the seam behind it, even though the onset verse oshb:Ezek.10.1 itself carries no mark; the close carries no parashah mark either (chapter 10 carries none at all, disclosed below), so the close-side seam rests on content alone — the coal-fire task is complete and the following verses shift from narrated action to sustained physical description.

P02-009.device_notes: Filed as salvation_oracle per the restoration promise that is the unit's burden (gather-and-return is stated here: MEASURED at oshb:Ezek.11.17, the oracle both gathers and gives the land — the consonantal skeleton carries וקבצתי אתכם מן העמים ואספתי אתכם מן הארצות and ונתתי לכם את אדמת ישראל, which the WEB renders “I will gather you from the peoples, and assemble you out of the countries where you have been scattered, and I will give you the land of Israel.” (web:Ezek.11.17) — and the “one heart… heart of flesh” (web:Ezek.11.19) promise stands alongside it, so the salvation_oracle filing rests on the device the unit actually carries); a one-sentence deviation is disclosed because the unit also carries a disputation-oracle color (the quoted Jerusalem claim at 11:15 is refuted before the promise is given), and the category is not read as free text beyond that single disclosure. No K/Q or paseq falls in this span.
P02-009.strongest_rejected_alternative: Holding 11:14-21 inside a single long 11:1-21 courtyard-and-oracle row, with the word-event at 11:14 disclosed only as internal texture, was weighed as an alternative reading. It was not taken because 11:14 is a strict word-event onset (not a bare transition) and the oracle's own addressee — the scattered exiles — differs from the courtyard men addressed in 11:1-13, which is enough of a class shift to justify treating it as its own formula-bounded row even while the wider vision frame stays open around it. A second rival sits inside this row and is weighed here as well: a seam at 11:16/11:17. This witness records a samekh after MT 11:15 and another after MT 11:16 (single witness), and because the witness enters each mark on the verse it stands after, both fall immediately before a verse that carries the long messenger formula כה אמר אדני יהוה — oshb:Ezek.11.16 and oshb:Ezek.11.17, two of that formula's 122 verses. Neither seam is licensed as a sub-onset, since a messenger formula opens one only if the people addressed change or the verse just before it finishes on a close-role formula. The addressee holds steady: the son-of-man address and the scattered exiles are named at 11:15 and nothing readdresses the oracle before 11:21. Nor does either preceding verse finish on a close-role formula — MEASURED on the pointed witness, MT 11:15 finishes לָ֥נוּ הִ֛יא נִתְּנָ֥ה הָאָ֖רֶץ לְמוֹרָשָֽׁה (oshb:Ezek.11.15) and MT 11:16 finishes בָּאֲרָצ֖וֹת אֲשֶׁר בָּ֥אוּ שָֽׁם (oshb:Ezek.11.16), while in 11:16 and in 11:17 alike the messenger formula stands at the verse's head after לכן אמר rather than at its end. A mark alone cannot stand in for that verse-final formula, so the two samekhs are disclosed for the paragraph structure they corroborate within the row, and the row rests on its strict word-event onset at 11:14 and its verse-final utterance close at 11:21 (MEASURED: נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה closes MT 11:21; oshb:Ezek.11.15, oshb:Ezek.11.21).

P02-017.boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.13.10 יַ֣עַן וּבְיַ֜עַן הִטְע֧וּ אֶת עַמִּ֛י לֵאמֹ֥ר שָׁל֖וֹם וְאֵ֣ין שָׁל֑וֹם וְהוּא֙ בֹּ֣נֶה חַ֔יִץ וְהִנָּ֛ם טָחִ֥ים אֹת֖וֹ תָּפֵֽל turns to the whitewash-wall metaphor “Because, even because they have seduced my people, saying, … and there is no peace.” (web:Ezek.13.10), with a fresh messenger formula at oshb:Ezek.13.13. Close: oshb:Ezek.13.16 נְבִיאֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל הַֽנִבְּאִים֙ אֶל יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וְהַחֹזִ֥ים לָ֖הּ חֲז֣וֹן שָׁלֹ֑ם וְאֵ֣ין שָׁלֹ֔ם נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהֹוִֽה ends with the utterance formula נאם אדני יהוה, naming “the prophets of Israel who prophesy concerning Jerusalem… visions of peace… and there is no peace” (web:Ezek.13.16); a pe follows this verse (single-witness), and an OSHB editorial note (single-witness apparatus) also falls here. Both sides: the onset continues the ch.13 indictment without an addressee change (so it is a sub-onset, not a fresh row-grade onset on its own merits) but the messenger-formula-plus-utterance-close bracket at the far end is clean and pe-corroborated.

P02-019.strongest_rejected_alternative: Opening the row at 14:2, the word-event proper, rather than at 14:1 is the rival that matters, and it is weighed below. On the rival's own side of the seam the evidence is strong: oshb:Ezek.14.2 carries the strict word-event formula, one of that formula's 39 verses. Behind it stands the elders' scene at oshb:Ezek.14.1, which carries no formula of its own. The parashah layer speaks for the RIVAL and not for this row, and it is written up that way: MEASURED in this witness, a pe is recorded on MT 14:1 (single witness), and the witness keys a break to the verse it follows, so it parts 14:1 from 14:2 — exactly where the rival would cut. Since no mark licenses a seam on its own, the corroboration is disclosed and left unadopted. The row opens at 14:1 all the same, on two stated grounds. First, the elders' scene at 14:1 is the setting the oracle answers, and it comes before the word-event at 14:2, so the row opens at 14:1. Second, a row under three verses is held only for a complete word-event unit, and the one-verse row at 14:1 that the rival's cut would leave behind is no such unit. Holding a licensed two-faced rival on stated grounds puts this row's boundary evidence at medium, and medium is the grade the row carries.

P02-020.device_notes: MT 14:14 and MT 14:20 both carry the Qere-adaptation editorial note class disclosed above, in addition to the ordinary ketiv/qere note at each verse (ketiv דנאל, qere דָּנִיֵּ֣אל (oshb:Ezek.14.14 and oshb:Ezek.14.20) — the shorter legendary-figure spelling against the fuller ‘Daniel’ reading); both disclosures are given at both verses since they are two independent single-witness apparatus facts about the same word. Paseq at 14:21 is count-only. oshb:Ezek.15.1 is cited above only as forward-side onset evidence for the seam; it is not a row here. Length disclosure: this row is 12 verses (MEASURED: web:Ezek.14.12-Ezek.14.23, tallied on the WEB face) against a 7-10 verse target length. The over-length is disclosed and carried rather than hidden: the four-scourge refrain list is never cut inside itself, and the one internal seam a reader might take, the messenger paragraph at 14:21, is weighed and held in the rejected alternative.
P02-020.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at oshb:Ezek.14.20, where a pe falls after the fourth triad refrain and immediately before the oracle turns from the hypothetical four scourges to their explicit application to Jerusalem (14:21-23), is the standing rival, and it is weighed here rather than passed over. MT 14:21 opens with a messenger formula: MEASURED on this witness's consonantal skeleton, oshb:Ezek.14.21 begins כי כה אמר אדני יהוה, and that verse is among the 122 verses that carry the long messenger formula. What it opens is nonetheless a paragraph, not a sub-onset, since a messenger sub-onset is granted only where the addressee changes or where the verse just before it ENDS on a close-role formula, and neither condition is met. Nothing marks a new addressee at 14:21 — MEASURED, the son-of-man address falls at MT 14:3 and MT 14:13 and at no other verse of this chapter, chapter 14 carries no set-your-face verse at all, and 14:21 is not opened by 'and you, son of man' — so what turns there is the subject, from a hypothetical land to Jerusalem, and not the person addressed. As for the second condition, the utterance formula in MT 14:20 does NOT reach the verse end: MEASURED, נאם אדני יהוה sits at characters 29 through 41 of an 81-character skeleton, the first character counted as 1 and both ends included, and the independent clause אם בן אם בת יצילו המה בצדקתם יצילו נפשם runs from there to the sof pasuq. So the pe on MT 14:20 is entered as support for the rival it favours and for no more than that: this witness records the break after MT 14:20, a mark cannot supply the verse-final close-role formula that the second condition asks for, and paragraph evidence informs while every licensed driver outranks it. The row carries on to its own verse-final utterance close at oshb:Ezek.14.23.

P05-005.boundary_rationale: Onset: 23:22 opens with the messenger formula directly addressing Oholibah by name (addressee shift from third-person dual narrative to second-person singular verdict), whole verse = "לָכֵ֣ן אָהֳלִיבָ֗ה כֹּֽה אָמַר֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ הִנְנִ֨י מֵעִ֤יר אֶת מְאַהֲבַ֨יִךְ֙ עָלַ֔יִךְ אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר נָקְעָ֥ה נַפְשֵׁ֖ךְ מֵהֶ֑ם וַהֲבֵאתִ֥ים עָלַ֖יִךְ מִסָּבִֽיב (oshb:Ezek.23.22)", corroborated behind by the samekh at 23:21 (the close of the prior unit). Close: 23:35, whole verse = "לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה יַ֚עַן שָׁכַ֣חַתְּ אוֹתִ֔י וַתַּשְׁלִ֥יכִי אוֹתִ֖י אַחֲרֵ֣י גַוֵּ֑ךְ וְגַם אַ֛תְּ שְׂאִ֥י זִמָּתֵ֖ךְ וְאֶת תַּזְנוּתָֽיִךְ (oshb:Ezek.23.35)" — a "therefore... because" verdict-summary still addressed to the same singular addressee, immediately before 23:36 shifts to a dual/plural addressee (both sisters together, weighed as the following unit's onset). CLOSE-SEAM MARK: MEASURED in the pointed witness, MT 23:35 is followed by a SAMEKH (setumah, closed section, single-witness). Because a mark is recorded on the verse it follows, this one stands on THIS row's close seam at 23:35/23:36 - not behind the onset and not mid-unit - so the close is corroborated on its near face by the mark and on its far face by the addressee-count shift at 23:36. A licensed text signal outranks a section mark, so the samekh is weak corroboration and decides nothing alone. One further measured fact is stated here without being acted on, because it bears on the rejected alternative rather than on this disclosure: MT 23:34 ends verse-finally on the utterance formula (oshb:Ezek.23.34), which means the messenger formula opening MT 23:35 stands right after a verse that ends on a close-role formula, and that alone licenses it as a sub-onset, so the 23:34/23:35 rival is a licensed, two-faced rival and not one defeated by addressee continuity alone. The close stays at 23:35 and the row stands at medium, the grade a row earns when it holds a licensed, two-faced rival on stated grounds; the question of that seam remains open.

P05-007.strongest_rejected_alternative: Two alternatives were weighed for MT 24:1, and a third inside the row. (1) Treating 24:1-27 as ONE unit (24:1 as the head of this collection's entire last movement, no further internal cut) — rejected because 24:15 carries its own full-form strict word-event onset (a hard seam in its own right) and a genre shift from mashal to sign-act, and both halves carry independent formula closes (24:14 and 24:27); collapsing them would also make one row far longer than the 7-10 verse target length. (2) Treating 24:1 as its OWN one-verse dated complex, separate from 24:2-14 — rejected because a dateline fused with a word-event in one verse is treated as a single onset that never splits, and because 24:3's dateline-day reference (verse-final words "שְׁפֹ֔ת וְגַם יְצֹ֥ק בּ֖וֹ מָֽיִם (oshb:Ezek.24.3)") ties the mashal directly to the date just given, with no seam between them. (3) Cutting at 24:8/24:9 - the alternative the Masoretic paragraph layer proposes, named and weighed here. What the rival's near face carries: MEASURED from the pointed Hebrew witness, MT 24:9 opens on the long-form messenger formula after a therefore-particle (oshb:Ezek.24.9). What its far face carries: MEASURED, the witness records a PE (petuchah, open section, single-witness) after MT 24:8 - and nothing else, because MEASURED from the pointed Hebrew witness MT 24:8 ends on a purpose infinitive (oshb:Ezek.24.8), with no utterance, recognition or I-YHWH-have-spoken signature anywhere in that verse. Whether it is licensed: it is NOT, since a messenger formula cuts only through a change of addressee or a close-role formula ending the verse before it. The first fails, because the addressee does not change - MT 24:6 already addresses the bloody city (oshb:Ezek.24.6) and MT 24:9 addresses that same city. The second fails, because the verse immediately before it does not END on a close-role formula, and a mark alone never supplies one. The stated ground on which this row holds: a section mark ranks below any licensed text signal, so the PE after MT 24:8 is weak corroboration, disclosed FOR the alternative it corroborates and not for this row, and it is outranked by the licensed drivers this row does rest on - the fused dateline-plus-word-event onset at 24:1 and the stacked I-YHWH-have-spoken plus utterance close at 24:14. So the 24:8/24:9 cut is a mark-only, paragraph-grade rival: weighed, disclosed and held, and, being mark-only, never fatal to this row's grade.
P05-007.device_notes: Dateline 24:1 counted among the book's 14 oracle datelines and in the 41-verse word-event any-form count; ABSENT from the strict 39-verse count because the year-month-day clause infixes between the two adjacency-anchor words the strict pattern requires; the 39/41/48/49-verse word-event counts are never blended. A single ketiv/qere pair sits at 24:2, its Qere reserved to the note layer rather than quoted here. Paseq at 24:6 (count-only, single-witness, unsourceable intra-verse position).

P05-008.device_notes: Paseq at 24:17 and 24:21 (count-only, single-witness, unsourceable intra-verse position). 24:24's recognition-pattern clause (2mp, Lord-YHWH variant, a member of the counted adonai-form class) is disclosed as mid-unit, paragraph-final rather than unit-final, since a refrain closes the unit it stands in, not necessarily the whole span, when the material after it is that same unit's own payoff (24:25-27). Samekh at 24:27 (single-witness) is both this unit's close and the parent collection's own close. Marks are disclosed in all three directions. MEASURED in this witness, MT 24:14 is followed by a PE (petuchah, OPEN section, single-witness), recorded on the verse it follows, so it stands behind this row's ONSET seam at 24:14/24:15. The interior direction carries a single-witness samekh after MT 24:24 (disclosed here) and the close direction the samekh after MT 24:27 (disclosed above), completing the three directions. A licensed text signal outranks a section mark, so the PE is weak corroboration; this onset rests on the full-form strict word-event formula at 24:15.

P06-005.boundary_rationale: Onset: 26:1 opens "וַיְהִ֛י בְּעַשְׁתֵּֽי עֶשְׂרֵ֥ה שָׁנָ֖ה בְּאֶחָ֣ד לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ הָיָ֥ה דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר" (oshb:Ezek.26.1) — an explicit month+day dateline (“In the eleventh year, in the first of the month”, web:Ezek.26.1, WEB) together with the PERFECT-form word-event, "הָיָ֥ה דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר" (oshb:Ezek.26.1), the 7-verse hayah family the dated oracles use after their dateline, a HARD seam and the strongest onset class in the book. In the WEB, “In the eleventh year, in the first of the month, Yahweh’s word came to me, saying,” (web:Ezek.26.1). 26:2 supplies the accusation, "בֶּן אָדָ֗ם יַ֠עַן אֲשֶׁר אָ֨מְרָה צֹּ֤ר עַל יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ הֶאָ֔ח נִשְׁבְּרָ֛ה דַּלְת֥וֹת הָעַמִּ֖ים נָסֵ֣בָּה אֵלָ֑י אִמָּלְאָ֖ה הָחֳרָֽבָה" (oshb:Ezek.26.2), quoting Tyre's own "Aha!" against Jerusalem. Close (both sides): 26:6 ends "וּבְנוֹתֶ֨יהָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה בַּחֶ֖רֶב תֵּהָרַ֑גְנָה וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה" (oshb:Ezek.26.6), the strict 3mp recognition formula, with a PE immediately after. Ahead, 26:7 reopens with a fresh messenger formula ("כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה הִנְנִ֧י מֵבִ֣יא אֶל צֹ֗ר…", oshb:Ezek.26.7) introducing Nebuchadnezzar's siege — a new speech unit against the same addressee, not an addressee change, which is why it is held as its own row rather than folded in here: the refrain at 26:6 closes THIS unit.

P06-011.boundary_rationale: Onset: 28:11 opens with the strict word-event formula, "וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר" (oshb:Ezek.28.11). 28:12 supplies the genre command, "בֶּן אָדָ֕ם שָׂ֥א קִינָ֖ה עַל מֶ֣לֶךְ צ֑וֹר וְאָמַ֣רְתָּ לּ֗וֹ כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה אַתָּה֙ חוֹתֵ֣ם תָּכְנִ֔ית מָלֵ֥א חָכְמָ֖ה וּכְלִ֥יל יֹֽפִי" — “Son of man, take up a lamentation over the king of Tyre” (web:Ezek.28.12, WEB) — the same imperative-plus-קִינָ֖ה anchor as 27:2, naming the addressee "king" (מֶ֣לֶךְ (oshb:Ezek.28.12)) rather than 28:2's "prince" (לִנְגִ֨יד (oshb:Ezek.28.2)). In the WEB, “Son of man, take up a lamentation over the king of Tyre, and tell him, ‘The Lord Yahweh says:” (web:Ezek.28.12). Close (both sides): 28:19 ends "כָּל יוֹדְעֶ֨יךָ֙ בָּֽעַמִּ֔ים שָׁמְמ֖וּ עָלֶ֑יךָ בַּלָּה֣וֹת הָיִ֔יתָ וְאֵינְךָ֖ עַד עוֹלָֽם" (oshb:Ezek.28.19) with a PE immediately after and no recognition/utterance/"I YHWH have spoken" formula present; the close pattern “You have become a terror, and you will exist no more.” (web:Ezek.28.19, WEB) mirrors MT 27:36's terminal clause in the CONSONANTAL Hebrew and not in the translation - MEASURED from the pointed Hebrew witness, the two verses end consonant for consonant on the same four words and differ only in the Masoretic pointing, feminine singular at MT 27:36 against masculine singular at MT 28:19, while the WEB renders MT 27:36 quite differently as “You have come to a terrible end, and you will be no more.” (web:Ezek.27.36, WEB); the exact mirror holds of the Hebrew consonants alone. Behind, 28:10 closed the prince-of-Tyre unit on the stacked "I have spoken" + utterance close and a SAMEKH; ahead, 28:20 opens a fresh strict word-event onset for the Sidon oracle.

P07-001.strongest_rejected_alternative: Three alternatives are weighed. (1) Ending the row at 29:6, where an extended (non-strict) recognition-type close occurs; rejected because 29:7 continues the same staff-of-reed image with no intervening onset, and because this chapter's own onset/close collision pattern places the true seam after 29:9, not 29:6. Two further readings are weighed. (2) Cutting at 29:7/29:8 - the alternative the paragraph layer proposes, and the witness's sectioning is disclosed for it: MEASURED, this witness places a SAMEKH (setumah, closed section, single-witness) after MT 29:7, recorded on the verse it follows, and that verse additionally carries one ketiv/qere pair, already disclosed in this row. What the rival's near face carries: MEASURED from the pointed Hebrew witness, MT 29:8 opens on the long-form messenger formula after a therefore-particle (oshb:Ezek.29.8), and with it a grammatical addressee shift - MT 29:7 addresses a masculine singular and MT 29:8 a feminine singular (oshb:Ezek.29.7, oshb:Ezek.29.8), that is, from Pharaoh to the land. Whether it is licensed: a messenger formula cuts as a sub-onset when its addressee differs from the one before or when the preceding verse ends on a close-role formula, and the first of those IS satisfied by that addressee change, so this rival is licensed and two-faced and is not dismissed. Its far face is nevertheless thin: MT 29:7 ends with no close-role formula, so the second would fail there and only the SAMEKH stands. The stated ground on which this row holds: the crocodile verdict's own refrain is the recognition formula at MT 29:9, and MT 29:10 restates the same charge as a fresh against-you cycle (oshb:Ezek.29.10); since a licensed text signal takes precedence over a section mark, the SAMEKH after MT 29:7 is weak corroboration, disclosed FOR this rival and not for this row. A licensed two-faced rival held on stated grounds leaves the boundary evidence at medium, where this row's grade sits. (3) Tiling MT 29:1-29:16 as ONE row, with the mid-verse WEB paragraph at 29:9 and the forty-years turn at 29:13 falling inside it. What supports it: MEASURED from the pointed Hebrew witness, no dateline and no word-event formula stands anywhere between MT 29:1 and the next dateline at MT 29:17; MEASURED in this witness, the only marks inside that stretch follow MT 29:7 and MT 29:12 (single witness), and NO mark stands on MT 29:9. And this row's own close has the weak mid-verse shape: MEASURED from the pointed Hebrew witness, the recognition formula in MT 29:9 ends at the etnachta and an INDEPENDENT causal clause with a finite verb fills the rest of the verse (oshb:Ezek.29.9) - unlike MT 29:6, whose words after its own recognition clause are a causal phrase built on an infinitive construct (oshb:Ezek.29.6), a dependent completion that grades as an ordinary licensed near-face signal rather than the weak mid-verse shape. The stated ground on which this row holds: MT 29:10 opens a fresh against-you verdict cycle restating the charge, so the collision is resolved at the verse boundary after 29:9. The weakness of the 29:9 close and the case for a single 29:1-16 row are disclosed rather than argued away; they are why this row is graded medium and not high.

P08-011.boundary_rationale: Onset: a fresh messenger formula at Ezek.36.13 כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה יַ֚עַן אֹמְרִ֣ים לָכֶ֔ם אֹכֶ֥לֶת אָדָ֖ם אתי וּמְשַׁכֶּ֥לֶת גויך הָיִֽית (oshb:Ezek.36.13) opens immediately after the refrain-grade close and samekh mark at oshb:Ezek.36.12, itself licensed as a cutting seam by the addressee change from the 2mp/2ms address of Ezek.36.1-Ezek.36.12 (‘you,’ the mountains) to the 2fs address (‘you,’ feminine singular, the land) that opens here — satisfying the seam condition from this side as well as from the close side. MT 36.13 and MT 36.14 are BOTH doubled-note K/Q verses (two Qere each): oshb:Ezek.36.13 carries ketiv 'אתי' / qere 'אָ֑תְּ' (‘you,’ feminine singular) and, as the unpointed last word of וּמְשַׁכֶּ֥לֶת גויך, a second ketiv read as qere 'גּוֹיַ֖יִךְ' ('your nation' plene); oshb:Ezek.36.14 carries ketiv 'וגויך' / qere 'וְגוֹיַ֖יִךְ' and ketiv 'תכשלי' / qere 'תְשַׁכְּלִי'. Of those four notes, morpheme separators are present in the K/Q layer -- and therefore stripped in the forms as rendered here -- only for the SECOND 36:13 note (2 separators) and the FIRST 36:14 note (4); the first 36:13 note and the second 36:14 note carry none in the layer at all, so nothing was stripped from either of them. MEASURED by counting the '/' morpheme separators in each of the two K/Q notes this witness carries at each of these verses: 36:13 measures [0, 2] and 36:14 measures [4, 0]. Ezek.36.14 also carries the utterance formula, and it recurs at Ezek.36.15 וְלֹא אַשְׁמִ֨יעַ אֵלַ֤יִךְ עוֹד֙ כְּלִמַּ֣ת הַגּוֹיִ֔ם וְחֶרְפַּ֥ת עַמִּ֖ים לֹ֣א תִשְׂאִי ע֑וֹד וגויך לֹא תַכְשִׁ֣לִי ע֔וֹד נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.36.15) (itself carrying one more K/Q pair on 'your nation') — a doubled internal utterance close. Close: a samekh mark follows Ezek.36.15, ending this sub-unit before the fresh, formally distinct word-event of Ezek.36.16.

P08-013.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 36.16-32 as one row rather than splitting at 36.23/36.24. Rejected for the same reason as the Ezek.36.16-Ezek.36.23 seam: at 36.23 the knowing clause and the utterance signature together fill the second half of that verse, the formula words sitting inside it rather than at its end, and what follows them as far as the final word is a dependent temporal infinitive and not an independent clause (oshb:Ezek.36.23) -- a formula whose remaining words merely complete its own clause is verse-final in effect, so this is a licensed close of the ordinary kind rather than the weak mid-verse case -- and 36.24 opens a fresh movement; the split keeps this row inside the 7-10 typical band (9 verses).

P10-005.boundary_rationale: Onset side: this seam carries no formula evidence of its own. 40:38 opens וְלִשְׁכָּ֣ה וּפִתְחָ֔הּ בְּאֵילִ֖ים הַשְּׁעָרִ֑ים (oshb:Ezek.40.38), “A room with its door was by the posts at the gates” (web:Ezek.40.38), with a bare vav, no transport verb and no measuring verb -- the topic shifts from gate architecture to the functional furniture used for slaughtering and washing the sacrifices, but nothing in the bytes marks the shift as a formula onset; it rests on content alone, following directly on the north inner gate's close at 40:37. The row continues through the singers' and priests' chambers (40:44-46, including the Zadokite priestly qualification, case-law texture inside a measurement row, disclosed) and closes at 40:47's וְהַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ לִפְנֵ֥י הַבָּֽיִת (oshb:Ezek.40.47) “The altar was before the house” (web:Ezek.40.47), a summary notice before 40:48's transport verb moves the tour into the temple building itself. Both sides of this row are held to a lower confidence than its neighbors precisely because neither its onset nor its close carries a tier-1 device.

P10-006.boundary_rationale: Onset side: 40:48's transport verb opens וַיְבִאֵנִי֮ אֶל אֻלָ֣ם הַבַּיִת֒ (oshb:Ezek.40.48) “he brought me to the porch of the house” (web:Ezek.40.48), marking entry into the temple building proper, distinct from every court and gate measured before it. A second transport verb follows at 41:1, וַיְבִיאֵ֖נִי אֶל הַהֵיכָ֑ל (oshb:Ezek.41.1) “He brought me to the nave and measured” (web:Ezek.41.1), disclosed here as continuous forward motion through one threshold sequence rather than a fresh row seam, since no formula or refrain close intervenes between the porch and the nave. The two-verse porch description (40:48-49) is held with the four-verse nave description (41:1-4) as one row rather than left as an under-three-verse fragment. Close side: 41:4 ends with וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י זֶ֖ה קֹ֥דֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִֽׁים (oshb:Ezek.41.4) “He said to me,” then “This is the most holy place” (web:Ezek.41.4), a genuine speak-formula close, before 41:5's fresh measuring verb turns to a new object, the house wall. This close carries a named speech formula rather than resting on content alone, unlike its neighbors on either side.

P10-008.boundary_rationale: Onset side: 41:12 turns to a different structure from the side-chamber circuit just closed, a change of measured object rather than a bare topic shift: וְהַבִּנְיָ֡ן אֲשֶׁר֩ אֶל פְּנֵ֨י הַגִּזְרָ֜ה פְּאַ֣ת דֶּֽרֶךְ הַיָּ֗ם (oshb:Ezek.41.12) “The building that was before the separate place at the side toward the west” (web:Ezek.41.12), confirmed by the fresh measuring verb וּמָדַ֣ד אֶת הַבַּ֔יִת (oshb:Ezek.41.13) that opens this row's own accounting of the building. The row carries the temple/separate-place/building triad each measured at a hundred cubits (41:13-14), the rear building and its galleries with a K/Q lexical variant on 'galleries' at oshb:Ezek.41.15 (ואתוקיהא, checked: a form variant, not a numeral), the side-chamber gallery structure (41:16-19), the cherubim-and-palm-tree decorative program running to above the entrance (41:18-20), the doorposts of the nave (41:21), the wooden altar-table with its own speak-formula notice, וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר אֵלַ֔י זֶ֚ה הַשֻּׁלְחָ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֖ר לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.41.22), its speech rendered “This is the table that is before Yahweh” (web:Ezek.41.22), opened by the 'spoke to me' root, distinct from the 'said to me' form at 41:4, the double doors of the nave and sanctuary (41:23-25), and the repeated cherubim-and-palm-tree pattern closing on the porch threshold. Close side: 41:26 ends וְצַלְע֥וֹת הַבַּ֖יִת וְהָעֻבִּֽים (oshb:Ezek.41.26), “the side rooms of the temple and the thresholds” (web:Ezek.41.26), and the next verse, oshb:Ezek.42.1, moves the tour out to the outer court with its double transport verb, וַיּוֹצִאֵ֗נִי … וַיְבִאֵ֣נִי -- a strong close by contrast, since the following onset is tier-1 even though this row's own onset rests on the measured-object change rather than a formula. The puncta extraordinaria at 41:20, וְקִ֖יר הַׄהֵׄיׄכָֽׄלׄ (oshb:Ezek.41.20), five instances of the upper dot U+05C4, are disclosed single-witness as intra-row texture on the decorative program's own close, not as boundary evidence.

P10-012.boundary_rationale: Onset side: 43:1's transport verb opens וַיּוֹלִכֵ֖נִי אֶל הַשָּׁ֑עַר (oshb:Ezek.43.1) 'he led me to the gate', beginning the named hard seam behind the closed measuring circuit, and the row immediately carries the glory-of-YHWH device twice (43:4, 43:5), part of the book's nine-verse departure/return arc for that idiom, alongside the river-Chebar inclusio at 43:3 (one of eight such verses tying this scene back to Ezek 1 and 10) and the prostration “and I fell on my face” (web:Ezek.43.3), one of five verses where the WEB reads “I fell on my face” (sweep: 5 verses). The row turns from vision report to direct address at 43:6-9: a voice from the house, the man beside the prophet, the 'son of man' charge naming YHWH's throne and footstool, and the polemic against the house of Israel's defilement of the sanctuary by royal corpses and high places. Close side: 43:9 ends the divine resolution וְשָׁכַנְתִּ֥י בְתוֹכָ֖ם לְעוֹלָֽם (oshb:Ezek.43.9) “Then I will dwell among them forever” (web:Ezek.43.9) immediately before the samekh (oshb:Ezek.43.9, single-witness) -- the first Masoretic paragraph mark since the pe at oshb:Ezek.39.29, ending a 103-verse unmarked stretch. This is the only row here whose close carries genuine parashah corroboration, and it is disclosed as single-witness even so.

P10-013.boundary_rationale: Onset side: 43:10 opens אַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֗ם (oshb:Ezek.43.10) 'you, son of man' directly after the samekh (single-witness) closing at oshb:Ezek.43.9 -- a near-form of the book's twenty-three-verse 'and you, son of man' sub-onset family, here without the leading vav, disclosed as such rather than counted against that sweep. It charges the prophet to show the house's pattern so Israel may be ashamed of its iniquities. Close side: 43:12 closes on a doubled envelope formula, זֹ֖את תּוֹרַ֣ת הַבָּ֑יִת ... הִנֵּה זֹ֖את תּוֹרַ֥ת הַבָּֽיִת (oshb:Ezek.43.12) “This is the law of the house” (web:Ezek.43.12) ... “Behold, this is the law of the house” (web:Ezek.43.12), repeating the title at the top and bottom of the same verse -- a strong lexical close-device, and the reason this three-verse span is held as its own row despite its length: the inclusio is a self-contained frame around 43:10-12 that a larger row would have to break through rather than around.

P10-014.boundary_rationale: Onset side: 43:13 opens with an explicit topic header, וְאֵ֨לֶּה מִדּ֤וֹת הַמִּזְבֵּ֨חַ֙ (oshb:Ezek.43.13), the vav-initial “These are the measurements of the altar” (web:Ezek.43.13), functioning as a list-onset in the same way such headers do elsewhere in the book, immediately after the doubled inclusio that closes 43:12. The row descends through the altar's base, lower and greater ledges, hearth and horns, in cubit-and-handbreadth units, one of which (43:15) carries two OSHB editors' notes, one marking an anomalous form and one recording a ketiv/qere decision the editors take with the Leningrad Codex against BHS, while the span's one K/Q note stands at 43:16. Close side: 43:17 ends with the steps 'toward the east' before 43:18 opens with the messenger formula, a clean tier-1 onset on the far side even though this row's own close rests on content completion rather than a refrain.

P11-010.boundary_rationale: Onset: a transport verb at Ezek.47.1 (“He brought me back to the door of the temple” (web:Ezek.47.1)) continues the vision after the hard seam at 46.24/47.1; a second transport verb follows immediately at 47.2, then the measuring sequence proper (3-5, four successive measured wadings) -- disclosed as a one-sentence category deviation from a pure vision_report, since the passage briefly carries temple_measurement's own device before returning to vision narrative. The row covers the river's rise from the threshold (1-2), the four measured wadings (3-5), the 'have you seen, son of man' address (6) and the return to the bank, the riverside trees and the healed sea (7-10), the unhealed swamps (11, a K/Q verse), and the closing description of the riverbank trees bearing monthly fruit (12), where the construction glossed 'its months' is disclosed as the book's final chodesh-root homograph, not a date formula. Close: the samekh recorded after Ezek.47.12 ends the row; the next verse, 47.13, opens with a fresh messenger formula addressed to the land-division topic -- a genre shift from vision to statute/allotment, the hard seam at 47.12/47.13.
P11-010.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at 47.5/47.6 to isolate the measuring circuit (47.3-5) as its own temple_measurement row. It is weighed and held on stated grounds. The rival's near face, Ezek.47.6, IS licensed: the verse is both a said-to-me verse and a guided-motion verse (וַיּוֹלִכֵ֥נִי, וַיְשִׁבֵ֖נִי), and it belongs to the closed 20-verse transport class, so a seam there would not be device-free. Its far face, Ezek.47.5, carries the fourth measure-verb occurrence and a content close (נַ֖חַל אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא יֵעָבֵֽר), with no close-role formula and no parashah mark, so the rival is one-faced rather than two-faced. The row holds against it on three stated grounds: Ezek.47.6's question looks BACK at the measuring just reported and its motion returns the prophet to the bank inside one scene rather than opening a new one; 47:1-12 reads as a single region with 47:6 inside it as interior texture; and the only further signal at 47:6 is the WEB's mid-verse paragraph, which is tier-4 and never corroborates a seam. Guided-motion verbs stand inside the measuring circuit, though not at its head: MEASURED over the pointed Hebrew witness, Ezek.47.3 does not BEGIN with a guided-motion verb (it opens בְּצֵאת הָאִ֥ישׁ) but does carry וַיַּעֲבִרֵ֥נִי later in the verse, and Ezek.47.4 carries that same form twice. Whether those tokens belong to the transport class that can open a row is an open question, so no membership claim is made here in either direction. The measuring sequence therefore remains texture inside the single river vision running 47.1-12, disclosed as a one-sentence category deviation rather than split into a separate row (oshb:Ezek.47.5, oshb:Ezek.47.3, oshb:Ezek.47.6).

P11-011.boundary_rationale: Onset: the messenger formula at Ezek.47.13 (thus says the Lord GOD, then “This shall be the border” (web:Ezek.47.13)) opens the land-division topic, a genre shift from the river vision behind it -- the hard seam at 47.12/47.13. The row covers the overall border statement and Joseph's double portion (13-14), the border's four sides in sequence, north/east/south/west (15-20), and the instruction to divide the land by lot including resident aliens (21-23). Close: the samekh recorded after Ezek.47.23 co-occurs with the utterance signature in the same verse -- a doubled close signal (formula close plus parashah mark on the same verse), recurring at 48.29.
